belongs_to: Let Us Do Q4 (a)-(i): the first picture, for the given fact 17 × 23 = 391 (the 'given information')
description: Panel 1 (top left of the figure group): array for 17 × 23. A double-headed horizontal arrow above the whole array carries the label '23' (centred above it); a double-headed vertical arrow to the left carries the label '17' (at its middle, left of the arrow). Drawn with base-ten blocks, every smallest cell is a square of side 1 unit with a dark outline; unit squares are pale orange/yellow unless stated blue. Layout of the whole array (same in all three panels): TOP BAND = two 10×10 'hundred' squares side by side (each 10 columns × 10 rows of unit squares, 100 cells, count verified), a gap, then three vertical 'ten' strips (each 1 column wide × 10 rows tall, 10 cells), each strip separated by a small gap. LOWER BAND (below the top band, small gap between rows) = rows made of two horizontal 'ten' strips (each 10 cells × 1 row) lined up under the two hundred-squares, and three single unit squares lined up under the three vertical strips. This panel: top band as described (2 hundred-squares + 3 ten-strips, height 10); lower band has exactly 7 rows (height 7), each row = 2 horizontal ten-strips + 3 single squares. Width = 10+10+3 = 23, height = 10+7 = 17. Total unit squares = 391 (2×100 + 3×10 in the top band = 230; 7 rows × (2×10 + 3) = 161; 230+161 = 391). ALL squares are the same pale orange/yellow; nothing is blue, no other colour.
